How to use this model
The left rail drives everything. Pricing, cooling, redundancy and density reset every view instantly.
Amber fields are inputs. Bids, alternates and estimate changes flow straight through to returns; accepted VE shows as the forecast after its deductive change orders.
Economics tie out. Construction → TDC → returns → IC recommendation reconcile on the QC ties.
Present & export. ▶ Present gives a full-screen view; Print / Excel builds board-ready packs, downloads the Excel model and loads an edited one.
An independent, illustrative cost-and-investment model of a representative 90 MW hyperscale campus in Northern Virginia — built to mirror a 74-sheet data-center cost, controls, program-management, data-governance and deal-presentation workbook across 35 linked views. Not affiliated with any actual named project. Select a section above or use the tabs; everything is live off the scenario controls.

Accepted VE is credited to the estimate by deductive change order once the redesign is priced; until then the BAC stays on the GMP basis and the VE-adjusted forecast shows the result. Aggressive ($41.8M) adopts every cost lever that preserves resiliency; Accept all ($68.8M) additionally takes the four High-risk resiliency reductions — UPS autonomy, cooling redundancy, standby-generation redundancy and fuel storage — the extra $27M. GC / CMAR bid evaluation — price is built up from the trade leveling below
RankBidder (CM / CMAR)GMP (leveled+fee)PriceSchedTechExpSafetyFinWeighted
Each GMP is the bidder's leveled trade prices plus an editable CM fee and contingency (set per bidder in the leveling table below); general conditions, bonds and insurance are trade lines, and owner soft costs and the owner's contingency sit outside the GMP. Every bid prices the accelerated schedule approved on 25 Jul 2026. Price score is derived automatically (lowest GMP = 10.0). The schedule / technical / experience / safety / financial scores are editable — type 0–10 in any cell. Adjust the weights above to re-rank.

Lifecycle carbon = embodied (cradle-to-completion) + operational over the assessment period. Operational carbon = IT load × PUE × hours × utilisation × grid intensity after renewable PPA. Capex-per-tCO₂e uses the live scenario's construction cost. Lever reductions are indicative and applied to the computed embodied / operational baselines.

Expected monetary value = probability × mean of the three-point (min / likely / max) impact. The P80 risk-based contingency comes from the analytical roll-up and a 10,000-trial Monte-Carlo simulation; carried contingency scales with the live construction estimate, and the coverage check re-evaluates live. Cumulative cash — plan vs actual vs forecast re-spread at the EVM rate
Plan (PV)Actual (AC)Forecast
The owner's monthly cost report at the program status date. Budgets scale with the live scenario; approved and pending change orders post to their CSI division; earned value and actual cost from the Delivery & controls EVM panel are allocated to divisions by planned value to date, weighted by progress and cost factors, so the divisions always tie to the program EVM. Forecast final cost = MAX(actual, committed + uncommitted × market premium + pending contingency-funded changes). Committed % for divisions with long-lead equipment is their trade scope under subcontract less the equipment still to be ordered on the procurement register; the acceleration premium approved on 25 Jul 2026 is priced into the awarded GMP, so it sits inside the division budgets. Mirrors the workbook's Cost Report tab.

Shocks apply to every month: NOI and the capital reserve scale with the NOI shock (and so does the forward NOI the sale is priced on); the cost shock scales the monthly uses and is called as equity; the exit cap moves by the shift. Debt and timing hold at the base case.

The investment committee's view of the deal, to the conventions institutional real-estate private-equity sponsors underwrite with: every cash flow on its month-end date and every return an XIRR; equity called as it is spent; a tiered LP / GP promote on LP-IRR hurdles; the fund's management fee and carried interest for the gross-to-net bridge; exit-cap × exit-year and NOI × cost grids; probability-weighted scenarios with a stress case; a refinance alternative; the sources of profit and seven IC gates. Everything re-runs from the sidebar, the lender's funding schedule, the development fee and the inputs above. Mirrors the workbook's PE Underwriting and PE Cash Flow (Monthly) tabs; illustrative and not affiliated with any sponsor.

Construction funding — monthly uses, equity first, and the interest-reserve test live · workbook Lender Package §2
Loan balanceCumulative equityLoan commitment
Monthly uses: the construction draw schedule (scaled to the live estimate), land plus entitlement and legal costs at closing, the utility contribution over its payment window, and other soft costs and contingency pro rata to construction. Interest accrues on the opening balance and is capitalized against the reserve budgeted in Total Development Cost. Equity first: the sponsor funds every use until its full commitment is in, then the loan draws; pro rata splits each month at the loan-to-cost.
Covenant stress tests — seven cases against DSCR, debt yield and LTV live · workbook Lender Package §3
Break-evens and covenant headroom
Lease-up — coverage before stabilization
YearNOIDebt serviceDSCRDSCR (IO)ShortfallRead
Each case shocks the stabilized NOI, the permanent rate, the exit cap and the development cost; debt service is the 30-year amortizing payment on the full loan. Break-even occupancy is the occupancy at which NOI just covers debt service, with operating expenses recovered pro rata to occupancy.
